EXPERIMENT DESIGN: Does embedding a chemical-feedback loop (p-logP, QED, binding affinity) align molecule generation with real-world distributions while preserving structural diversity and enhancing property scores?

==================================================================
0. RATIONALE
==================================================================
The question is causal-comparative: does embedding a property-driven feedback loop in a molecular generator (i) raise chemical-property scores, (ii) reduce molecular hallucination, (iii) preserve structural diversity (specifically not over-representing ultra-long carbon chains), and (iv) shift the generated distribution closer to real-world molecule distributions — simultaneously? The design isolates the feedback loop as the sole manipulated variable by holding backbone, training corpus, conditioning, and compute budget constant across arms, then measures the four outcomes on matched output sets. The ablation arm lets us attribute any affinity-driven gain specifically to the binding-affinity term rather than to p-logP/QED alone.

==================================================================
1. ASSUMPTIONS (locked a–g) + backbone caveat
==================================================================
a. Backbone: an RL-trained VAE (or equivalently a reward-shapeable score-based/transformer generator) is the working baseline. CAVEAT (per requirement): this is a working assumption, not a fact. The protocol is backbone-agnostic in its metrics; only the FEEDBACK INJECTION POINT shifts by backbone — (i) VAE/RL: reward R is used as the policy reward in a PPO/REINFORCE loop (or as a resampling score in best-of-N); (ii) diffusion: R becomes a classifier/score-guidance term added to the denoising score (∇log p(R|x)) or a guidance weight on a property-conditioned model; (iii) transformer (autoregressive): R is applied as a beam/sequence-level rescoring or as a reward in RL fine-tuning. The arms, DVs, and analysis are unchanged across these injection points; only step 2's mechanism note differs.
b. Molecular hallucination = operationally: (i) invalid/non-canonical SMILES, (ii) non-synthesizable structures (unrealistic valence, high synthetic-accessibility score), (iii) tautomer/stereochemical inconsistency.
c. Real-world alignment reference: ZINC drug-like subset (primary; large, purchasable, well-characterized), ChEMBL (secondary; bioactivity-anchored), plus the generator's own training set as a self-reference to detect drift away from learned chemistry.
d. Structural diversity = multi-metric panel: Bemis–Murcko scaffold distribution, MW and heavy-atom-count percentiles (P50/P90/P99), and an explicit ultra-long-carbon-chain fraction (molecules exceeding a length threshold, e.g., longest linear carbon run ≥ 12 or heavy-atom count beyond P99 of reference). "Preserved" = the feedback arm's scaffold coverage and heavy-atom percentiles do not significantly worsen vs. baseline and the ultra-long-chain fraction does not significantly increase.
e. Affinity oracle: a trained ML affinity predictor or a docking score, single fixed target for the base design (panel optional for multi-target). See sensitivity note in §5.
f. Compute/step budget: arms compared at matched sampling/step budget so property gains are attributable to the feedback loop, not extra compute.
g. Sample size: ≥10⁴ molecules per arm (see §3) to detect small diversity/alignment shifts.
No new assumptions beyond a–g were introduced.

==================================================================
2. DESIGN
==================================================================
Independent variable (IV): presence/composition of the chemical feedback loop in the generation pipeline.
Comparison arms:
  A — Baseline: generator with standard sampling, no feedback reward.
  B — Full feedback: reward R = w1·norm(p-logP) + w2·norm(QED) + w3·norm(affinity), gated by a hard validity constraint (invalid/unsynthesizable molecules receive zero reward and are not reinforced).
  C — Ablated feedback: reward R' = w1·norm(p-logP) + w2·norm(QED) (affinity term removed). C isolates the contribution of the binding-affinity component.
Weight choice: w1=w2=w3=1 on min-max or z-scored, target-tuned property scales by default; sensitivity to weights is a secondary check, not a primary arm.
Controls:
  - Backbone/training-corpus/conditioning/seed/compute held identical across A, B, C (the only deliberate difference is the reward).
  - Random seeds fixed and reported; multiple seeds (≥3) for the primary comparison to bound stochastic variance.
  - Reference sets (ZINC/ChEMBL/training) fixed and identical for all arms.
Dependent variables (DVs), computed per molecule then aggregated per arm:
  1. Property scores: p-logP (RDKit MolLogP), QED (RDKit), binding affinity (oracle, §5).
  2. Hallucination: validity fraction, synthesizability (SA score distribution), tautomer/valence consistency rate.
  3. Diversity: scaffold distribution (coverage + evenness, e.g., Gini/entropy), MW & heavy-atom percentiles (P50/P90/P99), ultra-long-carbon-chain fraction.
  4. Real-world alignment: distributional distance (kernel MMD on a molecular-fingerprint/property feature set, and property-histogram divergence) between the generated set and each reference (ZINC, ChEMBL, self-training).
Sample size: N = 10⁴ molecules per arm per seed (≥3 seeds → ≥3×10⁴ per arm). Justified by the need to resolve small shifts in P90/P99 percentiles, ultra-long-chain fractions (rare events), and MMD estimates; a pilot (10³) can refine N if variance is unexpectedly high.

==================================================================
3. PIPELINE / FEEDBACK-INJECTION STEP
==================================================================
1. Fix backbone, corpus, target condition, hyperparameters; log all so A/B/C differ only in reward.
2. Inject feedback per backbone (VAE/RL: PPO reward or best-of-N rescore; diffusion: score-guidance on R; transformer: sequence-level rescore or RL reward). Validity gate applied in all arms.
3. Sample N molecules per arm at matched step budget; record seeds.
4. Score properties (RDKit p-logP, QED; affinity oracle).
5. Compute hallucination metrics.
6. Compute diversity metrics (scaffold, MW/heavy-atom percentiles, ultra-long-chain fraction).
7. Compute alignment (MMD + histogram divergence vs each reference).
8. Run analysis (§4).

==================================================================
4. ANALYSIS PLAN
==================================================================
Per-metric arm comparisons (A vs B, and B vs C for the affinity attribution):
  - Continuous metrics (mean p-logP, QED, affinity, MMD, SA, percentiles): Welch t-test (or Mann-Whitney U if non-normal/heavy-tailed, e.g., SA and percentiles). Report effect size (Cohen's d / rank-biserial).
  - Proportion metrics (validity, ultra-long-chain fraction): two-proportion test (chi-square / Fisher or a two-sample proportion test with Hedges' g).
  - Scaffold coverage/evenness: compare distributions via a two-sample test on the evenness statistic; report scaffold-overlap (Jaccard) between arms.
Multiple-comparison control: FDR (Benjamini–Hochberg) across the primary metric family; Bonferroni reserved for the small set of headline pairwise claims.
JOINT (COMPOUND) HYPOTHESIS TEST — made explicit:
  The compound claim is the conjunction: (1) property scores rise (B>A on QED and, per target tuning, p-logP/affinity), AND (2) hallucination falls (B>A on validity + synthesizability), AND (3) diversity preserved (B not significantly worse on scaffold coverage/heavy-atom percentiles AND ultra-long-chain fraction not significantly increased), AND (4) alignment improves (B closer to ZINC/ChEMBL than A).
  - Conjunction test: the compound claim holds only if each component passes its individual test at family-wise/FDR-controlled significance AND the joint confidence region (e.g., a simultaneous confidence region via a multivariate normal bootstrap of the per-arm metric vector, or Bonferroni-adjusted per-component intervals that all exclude the null in the favorable direction) supports the conjunction. Report the conjunction as satisfied only if all four components are met; otherwise report which component(s) fail.
  - Affinity attribution: B vs C on the affinity DV and on alignment isolates the binding-affinity term's contribution (C carries p-logP/QED only).
  - Guard against multiplicity-eroded "significance": report the number of passing components (e.g., 3/4) and the joint CI, not just per-metric p-values.

==================================================================
5. BINDING-AFFINITY ORACLE — SENSITIVITY NOTE (highest execution risk)
==================================================================
If the oracle is weak or mis-specified, two things degrade: (i) the REWARD SIGNAL in arm B — the generator optimizes the oracle's score, so an inaccurate oracle lets the loop over-optimize an artifact (e.g., docking-score gaming / predictor bias) rather than true affinity, inflating the "affinity DV" without real chemical benefit; and (ii) the AFFINITY-DEPENDENT DV itself — the measured "binding affinity" no longer tracks real potency, so any B-vs-A or B-vs-C affinity gain becomes uninterpretable. The p-logP and QED terms (RDKit, well-defined) are unaffected, which is exactly why ablation arm C exists: if B's affinity gain vanishes when the oracle is down-weighted or swapped, the gain was oracle-driven.
Minimum quality bar before trusting the affinity term: for an ML predictor, a reported cross-validated R² ≥ ~0.6 (and calibration) on an out-of-distribution test set comparable to the generated space; for docking, an RMSD ≤ ~2.0 Å against a held-out experimental set for the target (or a documented benchmark concordance). If the oracle cannot meet this bar, the design degrades to the p-logP+QED-only claim (arm C as the primary), and the affinity DV is reported as exploratory rather than confirmatory.

==================================================================
6. FEASIBILITY
==================================================================
The design is executable as a paper-based protocol by a competent ML engineer/experimental chemist using standard open-source tools: RDKit computes p-logP, QED, SA, validity, tautomer normalization, scaffolds, fingerprints; MMD/histogram divergence are standard (e.g., sklearn/scikit-fda or a small kernel implementation); ZINC/ChEMBL subsets are public; the generator is a published, reproducible model. ENVIRONMENT CONSTRAINT (per requirement): the environment is CPU-only (gpu_enabled = false, no GPU) with network disabled and no pre-installed dependencies. The SCORING AND ANALYSIS stages (steps 4–8: all RDKit property/hallucination/diversity metrics, MMD and histogram alignment, and all statistics) are comfortably executable on CPU with standard open-source tools and require no GPU. The only stage that would normally use a GPU is model sampling/generation (steps 2–3); under the no-GPU constraint this is either (i) done offline on the researcher's own compute and only the output SMILES handed to this CPU analysis pipeline, or (ii) at the 10⁴×3 scale may be slow on CPU for some backbones — the design treats generation as an external, matched-budget step so the CPU analysis remains the executable, verifiable core. Highest execution risk remains the affinity oracle (§5).

==================================================================
7. LIMITATIONS
==================================================================
The backbone choice is a working assumption (a); results are not directly transferable across backbone families without re-injecting the feedback per §1. The affinity term is gated by oracle quality (§5); if the bar is unmet, the confirmatory claim reduces to p-logP/QED only. Distributional alignment is sensitive to the chosen reference (ZINC vs ChEMBL vs self-training) and to the feature space for MMD, so conclusions should be reported relative to the named reference. Ultra-long-chain detection is a fraction of a rare event, so its estimate has higher variance and requires the stated sample size. Finally, "preserves diversity" is a non-inferiority-style condition (not worsening), which is more conservative than a diversity-gain claim and should be framed accordingly. This is a design only; no experiment has been run.

2. DESIGN
==================================================================
Independent variable (IV): presence/composition of the chemical feedback loop in the generation pipeline.
Comparison arms:

  B — Full feedback: reward R = w1·norm(p-logP) + w2·norm(QED) + w3·norm(affinity), gated by a hard validity constraint (invalid/unsynthesizable molecules receive zero reward and are not reinforced).
  C — Ablated feedback: reward R' = w1·norm(p-logP) + w2·norm(QED) (affinity term removed). C isolates the contribution of the binding-affinity component.

  2. Hallucination: validity fraction, synthesizability (SA score distribution), tautomer/valence consistency rate.
  3. Diversity: scaffold distribution (coverage + evenness, e.g., Gini/entropy), MW & heavy-atom percentiles (P50/P90/P99), ultra-long-carbon-chain fraction.

3. Sample N molecules per arm at matched step budget; record seeds.
4. Score properties (RDKit p-logP, QED; affinity oracle).
5. Compute hallucination metrics.
6. Compute diversity metrics (scaffold, MW/heavy-atom percentiles, ultra-long-chain fraction).
7. Compute alignment (MMD + histogram divergence vs each reference).
8. Run analysis (§4).

==================================================================
4. ANALYSIS PLAN
==================================================================
Per-metric arm comparisons (A vs B, and B vs C for the affinity attribution):

5. BINDING-AFFINITY ORACLE — SENSITIVITY NOTE (highest execution risk)
==================================================================
If the oracle is weak or mis-specified, two things degrade: (i) the REWARD SIGNAL in arm B — the generator optimizes the oracle's score, so an inaccurate oracle lets the loop over-optimize an artifact (e.g., docking-score gaming / predictor bias) rather than true affinity, inflating the "affinity DV" without real chemical benefit; and (ii) the AFFINITY-DEPENDENT DV itself — the measured "binding affinity" no longer tracks real potency, so any B-vs-A or B-vs-C affinity gain becomes uninterpretable.
